title: Permission Sandbox: lightweight role authoring + impact preview
creator: Aria Patel
description:
Problem: Admins need a low-friction way to author roles and immediately understand the operational impact (who gains access, which routes change, and what audit entries will look like) before applying changes to production. Current role editor flows are heavyweight and risk-prone: edits are applied directly or require a separate staging org, leading to slow reviews and fear of regressions.

Proposed feature: 'Permission Sandbox' — a modal-first lightweight authoring surface embedded in the Console role editor that lets admins: create/modify a role draft, run an impact analysis against a selected scope (team/org/resources), preview the resulting access matrix and audit log entries, simulate member assignments, and either apply changes or export a reversible diff (with automatic audit annotations). The sandbox keeps a transient draft (viewable in UI) and emits a summarized diff that ties into the audit logging pipeline and the rollouts system (canary/apply policies).
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox can create a role draft with name, description, and granular permissions (read/write/admin) and save as draft
Impact analysis runs within 5s for orgs < 500 members, returns: affected routes/resources, sample list of members who gain/lose access, and example audit log entries
Simulated member assignment UI allows toggling a subset of members to validate direct/indirect access changes
Draft can be exported as a reversible diff file and is linkable (internal shareable URL) for approvals
Applying draft triggers a rollout option: immediate, canary (percentage), or scheduled — and writes an annotated audit event linked to the diff
Design passes accessibility review and fits Console layout patterns (no overflow at 1366x768)
Security review completed and data residency constraints noted for Private deployments
design_notes: UX principles: minimize cognitive load by surfacing only the delta vs baseline role; make 'who gets access' tangible via sample user list and resource heatmap; surface audit examples early to satisfy compliance reviewers. Primary entry points: 1) Role list -> 'Create in Sandbox' CTA, 2) Role detail -> 'Open Sandbox' for edits. Use a three-column modal layout: left = role editor (permissions tree), middle = impact summary (resources & counts), right = member simulator + audit preview. Persist drafts in a lightweight DB with TTL (30 days) and an optional pin-to-project. Avoid an extra page navigation. Use progressive disclosure for policy conditions (time-bound access, IP restrictions). Consider merging with existing 'role composer' but implement as separate MVP to reduce risk.
decisions: MVP will support only resource-level and route-level permissions (no attribute-based policies)
Sandbox drafts are persistent for 30 days by default and can be pinned for longer retention
Impact analysis uses cached sampling of membership for speed and labels results as 'sampled'
Export format: stamped JSON diff with metadata (author, timestamp, cycle id) to feed audit and release systems
tradeoffs: We chose a sampled impact analysis to meet latency targets — tradeoff is potential underestimation for extremely large orgs (>10k members). Full deterministic analysis will be an engineering follow-up and gated behind Dedicated/Private feature tiers due to compute cost. Inline simulation is limited to 200 members in MVP to keep the UI responsive. Linking drafts to the rollout system adds complexity to the control plane but provides safer apply paths.

User testing with 6 infra/infra-platform customers (Recruit via PM)
review_feedback: PM (Elena Ortiz): prefer 'preview-only' mode default to avoid accidental apply; require explicit 'Apply changes' with confirmation
Security (Luca Moretti): require audit annotation fields and KMS key id when in Private deployments
Eng (Priya Singh): recommend limiting default sample size to 100 members and surface a 'full analysis' async job option
